key_insight: A multi-domain EEG model that combines spectral, connectivity, and topological features can classify ADHD at the subject level more accurately than single-feature approaches.
clinical_relevance: This work supports the development of non-invasive, explainable EEG-based tools that may aid future ADHD screening and biomarker research.
method: Preprocessed EEG from 121 subjects and split it into overlapping windows for feature extraction.
Built 1,043 features across spectral, wPLI functional connectivity, and persistent homology domains, then reduced them to 110 using RFE.
Compared SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, and MLP with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and used SHAP/LIME for interpretability.
evidence_signal: The best model was SVM, with 80.17% accuracy, 80.95% F1-score, 80.14% balanced accuracy, 86.72% ROC-AUC, and 87.34% PR-AUC.
watch_item: Performance was based on a relatively small single-study cohort, so external validation and real-world robustness testing are still needed.
paper_title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
